---
address: maldives.geo.postalCode
description: Real Maldivian postcodes — five digits, leading zeros kept. The structure is two digits of atoll zone and three of place: 02040 is in Haa Dhaalu, 19020 is Hithadhoo in Addu, 20026 is the head office of Maldives Post on Boduthakurufaanu Magu in Malé. The leading zero is not decoration and the ZERO ZERO is not a bug: Alif Dhaalu, the southern half of Ari Atoll, holds the whole 00 zone — Mahibadhoo is 00040 and Dhangethi is 00060 — because it was created in 1984 after 01 to 19 had been handed out, so a postcode field typed as an integer silently deletes an atoll. See maldives.geo.postalCodeZone. The two halves of the list behave differently. Atoll codes are sparse and almost all end in 0, one per inhabited island or resort, stepping 010, 020, 030 through the atoll from north to south; Malé codes are dense and go down to the individual street, which is why the 20 zone alone accounts for more than three quarters of the values here. The list is what could be verified against published registers rather than every code in existence: Gaafu Alif, whose zone is 16 by position between Laamu at 15 and Gaafu Dhaalu at 17, had no island-level codes in any register consulted and is represented by its zone alone rather than by invented five-digit codes, and the Villimalé (21), Hulhulé (22) and Hulhumalé (23) zones are likewise declared but not enumerated.
